comparison_with_iteration_1.iter2_with_skill: 86.7% (10 assertions, much harder set — includes forbidden patterns, jargon check, business transformation, credibility section)
comparison_with_iteration_1.note: Assertions are stricter in iter2 — direct comparison with iter1 pass rates is misleading

analyst_observations: with_skill has much lower variance (stddev 0.094 vs 0.205) — more consistent output quality
with_skill passes ALL structural assertions (A1, A3, A7, A8) on every eval — the skill enforces structure perfectly
The skill's main weakness: it still leaks forbidden patterns in 2/3 evals (A6) — 'en 90 secondes' and 'Aucun prérequis' slipped through despite explicit forbidden list
without_skill leaks tech jargon (MCP, API) in messages in 2/3 evals — the skill eliminates this completely (A10: 100% vs 67%)
Eval 3 FluentCRM without_skill scored 100% — the formation use case is naturally credible and structured, so the skill adds less value here
The biggest skill advantage is on the hardest case (eval 1 Google Ads): 80% vs 50% — a +30% gap on the most technical offering
Token usage is ~26% higher with skill (~38K vs ~30K) — the 9-step structure produces more thorough output but costs more
